title: Reservation stress test and fallback budgeting - Nov 2027
content:
Purpose:
Run multiple reservation stress scenarios across contracts and regions to validate our fallback budgeting rules, burst credit consumption, and eviction ordering. Deliverable: per-contract recommended buffer, burst allowance, and explicit fallback model variant mapping to meet 99th percentile SLA during 2x and 3x demand spikes.

Summary conclusions (top of sheet):
- Under a 2x sustained spike for 72h, contracted A100-equivalent reservations should have a minimum 12% buffer to avoid cross-tenant shedding in eu-west and us-west clusters.
- For 3x spike (short 6h peaks), burst credit pool covers ~70% of events if we cap single-contract burst to 40% of its reserved GPUs. Any higher and we must engage regional emergency re-routing to another region or fallback to quantized model variants.
- Recommended policy change: add a per-contract burst cap + global region burst ceiling, and a new prioritized fallback list per SLA tier to reduce tail latency incidents.

Sheet: Reservation stress test snapshot (table). Columns separated by tab for readability.

Contract ID	Customer	Region	Reserved GPUs (A100-eq)	Buffer % (current)	Utilization target	Observed 2x peak util	Observed 3x peak util	Burst cap % (proposed)	Burst credit pool used (2x)	Burst credit pool used (3x)	Fallback variant	SLA tier	Notes
RN-1721	MosaicAI	us-west	48	8%	70%	95%	>100%	40%	24 GPUs	34 GPUs	quant-8bit-v2	gold	High realtime demand; schedule canaries on Nov 25.
RN-1840	HealthSight	eu-west	32	10%	65%	90%	~110%	35%	11 GPUs	18 GPUs	quant-4bit-latency	platinum	Regulated data; prefer region-local fallback.
RN-1902	LexFlow	ap-south	12	5%	60%	82%	96%	30%	2 GPUs	4 GPUs	kv-cache-prime	standard	Burst usage concentrated M-F 08:00-10:00 local.
RN-2008	RetailGrid	us-east	96	15%	75%	98%	>120%	40%	45 GPUs	82 GPUs	sharded-quant-v1	enterprise	Holiday test scenario causes sustained load.
RN-2117	EduAssist	eu-central	16	6%	60%	85%	103%	25%	3 GPUs	5 GPUs	quant-8bit-v2	standard	Short training bursts observed during term starts.
RN-2255	FinPulse	us-west	64	12%	70%	97%	115%	30%	19 GPUs	37 GPUs	quant-4bit-latency	platinum	Nightly backtests cause tail spikes.

Interpretation notes:
- "Reserved GPUs" reported in A100-80GB equivalent. Conversion used: V100->0.45, A100-40GB->0.8, A10->0.09 (see conversion tab).
- "Observed 2x peak util" is the simulated utilization for a sustained 48-72h 2x demand multiplier. "3x peak util" is 6h short spike simulation. Values >100% indicate simulated demand above reserved capacity (would require bursting or shedding).
- "Burst credit pool used" is the number of A100-eq GPUs that would be drawn from the regional burst pool under current policy.

Simulated scenarios and assumptions (methodology):
- Traffic profiles pulled from 6-week rolling window, weighted for seasonality. Nightly batch jobs were modeled separately to avoid skewing realtime SLA numbers.
- Latency-sensitive requests are pinned to platinum/gold SLA lanes and prioritized in allocation policy; bursts for these customers have a stricter cap (30-35%) in the proposals.
- Burstable pool sizing: regional pool = sum(ceil(reserved * 0.2) for tenant in region) but we propose dynamic scaling where pool <= 20% of region capacity by default, can scale to 30% under emergency.
- Eviction ordering: (1) standard -> (2) gold -> (3) platinum. Within same SLA, use oldest-preemptible allocation.

Recommended changes (actionable):
1) Add per-contract burst cap field to reservation object in allocator (API change): burst_cap_pct. Default 30% for standard, 35% gold, 40% enterprise.
2) Implement a regional burst ceiling: cannot allocate >30% of region capacity to burst credits without operator override.
3) Create explicit fallback mapping in contract metadata: primary_model -> [fallback_quantized_variant, fallback_sharded_variant] with per-fallback expected latency multiplier.
4) Run a production canary (us-west) on Nov 25: target customers RN-1721 and RN-2255 with 2x sustained load for 36h to validate metrics pipeline and automated rollback.
5) Update customer-runway reports to include burst_consumption_ratio and time_above_reserved metrics.

Risk matrix (short):
- If burst pool exhausted during global event (e.g., holiday flash sale), lower-tier customers will face immediate shedding; mitigants: preemptive customer notifications, cross-region re-route, emergency temporary increases for platinum customers.
- Quantized fallback increases error rates for critical customers; mitigants: per-contract acceptance tests and rollback hooks in rollout pipeline.

Appendix (selected calculations):
- Example: RN-2008 (RetailGrid): reserved 96 A100-eq, buffer 15% -> cushion = 14 GPUs. 3x short spike demand est = 288 demand units -> deficit = 288 - 96 - 14 = 178 A100-eq -> burst cap 40% allows 38 GPUs from contract itself, regional pool used = remaining 140 GPUs (if available).
- Regional pool sizing example (us-west): total reserved = 1500 A100-eq -> default pool = 300, emergency ceiling = 450.

Open questions (for infra/product sync):
- Product: should we expose burst_cap_pct to customers in Console? Pros: transparency; Cons: customers may game request patterns.
- SRE: acceptable time-to-reconfigure region burst ceiling during live incidents? Need runbook changes.
- Sales/CS: do platinum customers accept quantized fallback as part of SLA or do we require warm standby instances?

Next steps and owners:
- Allocate engineering spike to implement burst_cap_pct + metadata mapping (owner: Rohit) due 2027-12-15.
- Schedule canary run with solutions engineering (owner: Maya) planned 2027-11-25; create runbook and rollback checks.
- Update customer-runway dashboard to include burst metrics (owner: Lucas) due 2027-12-02.

Revision history:
- 2027-11-08: initial draft (Sasha)
- 2027-11-15: added 3x spike simulations and new escape analysis (Rohit)
- 2027-11-22: consolidated fallback mapping and canary dates (Maya)

End of sheet.
